title: When visibility bugs appear, and what volatile adds

blocks.text: Questions on what this page has just taught. Choose one answer for each.

questions.stem: Per this page, why can a visibility bug pass every test and then show up only after an application has run for minutes?

options.text: The JIT compiles the method only once it runs hot, and may then keep the read in a register
options.says: The page says a bug can appear only after minutes of running, once the JIT compiles the method and hoists loop-invariant reads into registers.

options.text: The CPU caches drift apart over time, until the hardware stops keeping them coherent
options.says: The page says CPU caches themselves are kept coherent by the hardware; the usual culprit is the JIT.

options.text: The interpreter starts to skip reads from main memory once the program has warmed up
options.says: The page says that in interpreted mode the JVM reads from main memory on every access.

origin.section: 1. JIT compiler hoisting and the -Xint flag

questions.stem: Per this page, what does declaring a long field volatile add on a 32-bit JVM, beyond visibility?

options.text: Each compound update of the field, such as count++, becomes atomic
options.says: The page says volatile does NOT provide atomicity for compound operations like i++.

options.text: Each plain read and each plain write of the field becomes atomic
options.says: The page says long and double reads and writes may tear on 32-bit JVMs and that volatile guarantees atomic reads and writes.

options.text: Each access to the field is served from a register, which is faster
options.says: The page says the bug volatile prevents is the JIT keeping a value in a register; a volatile read fetches the latest value every time.

origin.section: 3. 64-bit value tearing for long and double

concepts: A visibility bug may not show in interpreted mode and appear only after the JIT compiles the code, so passing tests prove nothing.
Plain long and double reads and writes may tear on 32-bit JVMs, and volatile makes them atomic.
